## Highlights

- **Security fix:** only Owners and Admins can read the organization's [Enterprise SSO](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/enterprise-sso) settings. Before this release, Members, Editors and Developers could read them too, through `GET /api/app/sso/config`, although only Owners and Admins could change them. That read now refuses them with 403, as changes already did, and **Settings › Enterprise SSO** asks for the settings only for a role that may read them.
- People who sign in through single sign-on stay signed in while they work. On a deployment that leaves `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` unset, an organization's [**Session idle timeout**](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/policies-and-limits#configure-sign-in-limits-separately) signed them out one idle window after sign-in, however actively they worked: Tale takes a session's last use from a time that only the session's renewal wrote, and a single sign-on session is first renewed some 23 days after sign-in. Tale now records the use whenever it authorizes a request from the browser, at most once a minute, so a session left idle is still signed out one window after its last use ([#5249](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5249)).
- **Log out** and **Sign in again** stay available to a person who signs in with a passkey on Tale's own sign-in page, also when they enrolled the passkey while a trusted proxy had signed them in. Such a passkey carries the role the proxy asserted, and Tale read every session that carried a role as one the proxy opened, which offers no sign-out. Tale now marks the sessions that [trusted headers](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/authentication) open, and hides the two buttons only for those ([#5259](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5259)).
- Skills with files of up to 4 MiB, the most a skill upload takes per file, now work in chat, in project agents' tasks and in automations' agent and script steps. Copying a skill into the sandbox took at most 1 MiB per file, so a skill with a 1.2 MB template uploaded fine and then failed in chat with "run_code failed unexpectedly". When a file cannot be copied, the message names the file, its size and the limit: chat reads "A file couldn't be copied into the sandbox" and tells the model whether trying again can help, and a task or automation run fails naming the file and the limit. The [skills pages](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/workspace/skills#import-an-existing-bundle) now state a bundle's limits: 512 files, 4 MB per file and 32 MB in all ([#5177](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5177)).
- A worker that runs [project agents](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/project-agents)' tasks every hour no longer fills the server's disk. Such a worker was never idle long enough for its workspace cleanup, so it kept every checkout its runs made until new sessions waited for free disk space. Each task now works in a directory of its own, `/agent/workspace/tasks/<task id>`, which the agent's instructions name. At the start of each run, while the run goes on, the worker deletes the directories of up to five tasks that are done, cancelled, archived or deleted, or unchanged for 7 days, oldest first. It never deletes the directory of the run's own task or of a task with a queued or running run ([#5255](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5255)).
- A scheduled automation no longer pauses itself because a connector's service was busy or briefly failing. When the service behind Confluence, Discord, Forgejo, GitHub, Gmail, Google Drive, Jev decisions, Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams, Shopify, Slack, Tavily or Twilio answers 429, the step now fails as rate limited, and a 5xx fails with the service's status. Neither counts toward the five failures in a row that [pause a schedule](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/triggers#when-a-schedule-pauses-itself), where both counted before. Google Drive file downloads and Outlook attachment downloads read the same way ([#5274](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5274), [#5277](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5277)).
- On **Settings › Connectors**, a refused credential save or OAuth app change is worded in English, German or French: the message names the connector as its card does, settings by their labels, and secret fields and sign-in methods as the dialog labels them. It showed the server's English in every language ([#5222](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5222)).
- On **Settings › AI providers**, a provider whose model listing fails says why in English, German or French on its credential row, in **Check models** and in the **Refresh catalogs** report: that the endpoint could not be reached or did not answer in time, that it refused the API key or needs one, or that it answered with a server error. The server's own words follow in parentheses. These messages were in English in every language; see [recover a missing or failing model](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/providers#recover-a-missing-or-failing-model) ([#5223](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5223)).
- Under **Settings › Data residency › Embedding model**, choosing another provider clears the credential, the model and the vector width, and **Save** stays off until a model is chosen. Before, **Save** stayed on over the emptied fields, and a click only said "Fix the highlighted fields". A model whose catalog states no width shows the width's error beside the field, instead of a placeholder width that read like a value ([#5182](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5182)).
- **Save** follows a form's values when Tale fills a field itself. Under **Settings › Data residency**, turning on **Force path-style (MinIO/R2)** as the first change to **External S3** storage no longer leaves **Save** on over an empty **Region** and **Bucket**. On **Settings › Enterprise SSO**, **Save** no longer stays off over valid values after a protocol switch fills an emptied display name, or when the client ID you asked to reveal arrives after you edited the form, and the field's "required" error clears ([#5260](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5260)).
- A chat's model pick that its provider no longer lists, because an admin changed the provider's allowlist or removed its credential, now falls back to the default even when another provider still lists the same model, as a pick that no provider lists already did. Before, the closed picker showed the model with no row checked, and sending started the turn on the old provider, which refused it. The second column of an **Arena Mode** duel falls back the same way ([#5269](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5269)).
- The chat composer's picker keeps one width, 20rem (narrower on small screens), instead of changing width as you scroll its model and skill lists. A row cut short shows its full text in a tip on hover or keyboard focus, and the provider after each model, the **Auto** description and the skill descriptions now reach the 4.5:1 contrast of WCAG AA in the light and dark themes ([#5140](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5140)).
- While the next page loads, the tabs and the **Settings** panel mark the page still shown, not the one being opened. A first visit to **Knowledge entries**, **Websites**, **Products** or **Contacts** shows its rows without loading placeholders first, and opening **Websites** no longer fetches its count, list and search readiness twice ([#5198](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5198)).

## Upgrade notes

- No migration file is added, and the API contract stays at `3.52.0`.
- At start, the backend adds the nullable column `signedInByProxy` to the sign-in `session` table, in Better Auth's own schema step, and then, once per database, marks every session that carries a trusted role as signed in by a proxy. It logs how many it marked: "marked N session(s) carrying a trusted role as signed in by a proxy". So the sessions that trusted headers opened keep offering no **Log out**. A passkey sign-in from before the upgrade, with a passkey enrolled behind the proxy, is marked too and keeps hiding **Log out** until it ends; the next sign-in offers it ([#5259](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5259)).
- Skill files over 1 MiB need this release's sandbox runtime image. `tale deploy` starts sessions from it. A deployment that sets `SANDBOX_RUNTIME_IMAGE` itself, on [Kubernetes](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/kubernetes) or with [your own Compose file](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/own-compose), keeps it on the same release as the other images, as on every upgrade. An older runtime refuses such a file, and the message names the file, its size and the limit ([#5177](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5177)).
- A project agent's worker now deletes the directories under `/agent/workspace/tasks/` of tasks that are closed or unchanged for 7 days. What must outlive a task belongs on its branch or among its deliverables, as the [project agents](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/project-agents) page says. Checkouts elsewhere in a worker's workspace, such as those that earlier runs made, are not touched ([#5255](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5255)).
- While a browser session is in use, the backend writes its last use to its `session` row at most once a minute. A failed write is logged with `[session-use]`, and the request still goes through ([#5249](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5249)).
- No configuration, limit or sign-in setting needs to change beyond these: the other fixes take effect with the new images.
